newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 18.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
FIND SOLUTION BY APRIL 21: PRESIDENT

President Shankar Dayal Sharma took the initiative to resolve the political crisis by holding separate meetings with leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPM) and Congress. The president was understood to have conveyed to the three leaders that he wanted an early end to the crisis, preferably before parliament meets on April 21. The president's decision to summon the three leaders was likely to put both the Congress and the United Front leaders under pressure, more so because BJP had made known its opposition to the idea of the United Front being invited again to form the government.
The Pioneer
CONGRESS YIELDS WITH 'VIA MEDIA' LETTER TO UNITED FRONT

The Congress party despatched a second letter to the United Front (UF), paving the way for a new government. This followed the president's initiative in exploring options for the formation of a government. The new letter virtually conceded the United Front's claim to form the government and assured support to the UF provided it changed its leader. Party sources said the second letter was a face-saver since the Congress could not withdraw its claim letter as it would have been an embarrassment. The UF had earlier demanded the Congress withdraw its letter to the president, staking claim to form the government.
The Times Of India
STABILITY WARRANTS PEACE WITH CONGRESS: MOOPANAR

Some sort of a compromise between the Congress party and the United Front (UF) coalition would have to be worked out for the formation of a stable government. This was stated by G.K. Moopanar, one of the likely successors to the outgoing prime minister. Moopanar said he would decide on accepting any offer for the top post only after a decision was taken by the UF steering committee on the leadership question.
The Economic Times
GOVERNMENT ASKED TO SELL STAKE IN FIVE UNITS

The Disinvestment Commission recommended a strategic sale of government equity in five state-owned firms (PSUs) and a public offer in the case of a sixth. The units recommended for strategic sale were Bharat Aluminium, Bongaigaon Refinery and Petrochemicals, Hindustan Teleprinters, Indian Telephone Industries and Madras Fertilisers. For Manganese Ore (India), the commission recommended a capital restructuring followed by a 49 percent public offer for small investors and employees. Gas Authority, ITCL and Modern Foods were recommended for diversification in February.
NHB MAKES CONDITIONAL PAYMENT TO ANZ

The dispute between National Housing Bank (NHB) and ANZ Grindlays Bank appeared to have blown over. The foreign bank gave an assurance to the special court that it would repay 9.12 billion rupees with interest if the arbitration award was set aside. On its part, NHB despatched a 9.12 billion rupee cheque drawn on the apex bank to ANZ Grindlays. ANZ's decision followed an order by the special court on a miscellaneous petition filed by NHB asking for the court's intervention on the issue.
COMPANIES BILL TO INCLUDE NORMS FOR NON-VOTING SHARES

The draft Companies Bill, which was expected to be presented to members of parliament on Monday, would include new provisions relating to non-voting shares. Sources said the draft would be circulated among the members and later made public for a debate. This bill was to be presented during the monsoon session of parliament and the Income-Tax Bill, which was yet to be formulated, in the winter session. The future of the draft bill, based on the recommendations of the expert panel set up to review the Companies Act, would depend on the political scenario.
INVESTMENT OUTFLOW IN APRIL-JAN STOOD AT 6.86 BLN RUPEES

The total investment outflow from India during April-January 1996/97 stood at $196 million (6.86 billion rupee). Among these, majority of the investments were in trading concerns, official sources said. Investments were made in textiles, garments, marine products, leather and electrical goods. In the manufacturing sector, approvals were given for yarns and textiles, pharmaceuticals, garments, cement and sugar. A number of approvals were also given for software development and related fields. Countries where investments were proposed include Britain, the United States, Germany, Singapore, Mauritius, UAE, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Russia and Malaysia.
Financial Express
RINGING VOTE OF CONFIDENCE FOR CREDIT POLICY

The monetary policy for the first half of the current fiscal year took the markets by storm as forward premia crashed and the rupee strengthened. Gilt prices also reacted in line with expectations of cheaper money. On the bourses, bank shares led the rise in the index. The most dramatic change came in the forward market for dollars, where six-monthly premia dipped to 4.9 percent from the pre-credit policy high of 6.1 percent. The spot dollar gained 0.05 rupee but yields on medium and long term securities crashed. Call rates continued to rule at below 0.5 percent as the system was flush with funds, while 91-day T-bill yields crashed at the latest weekly auction.
CANADIAN COMPANY TO SEET UP ALUMINIUM COMPLEX

Continental Resources, an internationally active Canadian mining company, will set up a greenfield integrated aluminium complex in Orissa. This would be the first aluminium complex in India promoted solely by a foreign company. Continental Resources proposed to invest around $2,000 million to set up a one million tonne alumina refinery, a 250,000 tonne smelter and a 500 megawatt captive power station as part of the complex.
SIEMENS PUBLIC COMM SETS 13 PCT MARKET SHARE TARGET BY 2000

Siemens Public Communication Networks (SPCNL) set an enviable target of taking a 13 percent share of India's growing telecom market with a growth prospect of 10 billion rupees in the next three years. The new company was a joint venture between Siemens AG and Siemens Limited on a 70:30 basis. SPCNL would concentrate in the field of cellular and basic services. The company did not have plans to enter into paging. The company would draw on the considerable financing resources of the parent company to meet its funding requirements.
BONGAIGAON REFINERIES, OIL SET TO MERGE

Bongaigaon Refineries and Petrochemicals (BRPL) is slated for merger with Oil India (OIL) in the first such reorganisation of state-owned oil companies. The proposed entity would notch net worth of over 23 billion rupees and turnover of around 20 billion, as per 1995/96 estimates. The Petroleum Ministry planned to create a company out of the merged entities with sufficient muscle to become a key player in the oil sector in the region. The proposed amalgamation was in accordance with the recommendations of the expert committee report which called for a drastic overhaul of state-owned oil companies to cope with increased international competition.
Business Standard
UNIT TRUST TOLAUNCH $150 MLN OFFSHORE DEBT FUND

Unit Trust (UTI) was set to launch India's first offshore debt fund. The fund, pegged at $150 million, would be launched next month end. UTI was currently in the process of tying up with Nomura International of London to market the fund to institutional investors. The offshore fund, which would be based in Mauritius, would be a close-ended scheme for the first three years and then turn open, an UTI official said.
WORLD BANK PUTS LOAN FOR PUNJAB ON HOLD

The World Bank has stopped processing a $250 million to $300 billion loan to the Punjab government for financing a rural water supply scheme. The World Bank managing director said the decision was taken following the state government's announcement after its recent victory in the elections that water and power would be supplied free to all farmers. Implementation of the election promise of providing free water and power was diametrically opposed to what the government had given the World Bank as a policy statement, he said.
LIGHT COMMERCIAL VEHICLES SALES DIP 5.5 PCT

Reflecting the sluggish trend witnessed by the automobile sector in 1996/97 (April-March), sales of light commercial vehicles dropped by 5.5 percent to 76,140 units from 80,555 units in the previous year. However, sales of passenger cars, utility vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles (HCVs) saw a modest growth. Passenger car sales rose 18.8 percent to 374,829 units from the 315,471 units sold in 1995/96. HCVs, too, witnessed an 18.9 percent growth in sales in 1996/97 with 140,986 units being sold against 119,289 units in the previous year. The utility vehicles market witnessed the maximum growth with sales growing 30.72 percent to 132,639 units from 101,466 units in 1995/96. Sales growth in the passenger car segment was mostly on account of new entrants in the domestic market.
HOMEOPATHY MAJOR WILLMAR SCHWABE SETS UP BASE IN INDIA

The Indian homeopathy industry may be heading for a shake-out under the heat of foreign competition. This was more so with Germany-based homoeopathic medicine company Dr Willmar Schwabe Arzneimittel GmbH inaugurating its manufacturing plant near Delhi. Its products were hitherto imported from Germany. The German firm, with a global turnover of $400 million, now has over 60 percent of the import segment of the Indian market. The retail market for homoeopathic medicines in the country was estimated at 2.5 billion rupees, which at present, was dominated chiefly by some 200,000 practitioners, more than any other country.
The Observer
EXPORTERS RUSH FOR FORWARD COVER

Expecting the forward premium in the long term market to come down, exporters rushed for six-month cover. Foreign exchange dealers reported numerous enquiries from exporters for September and October in expectation of the forward premium in the long term market to come down. It was perceived the rupee would strengthen, since the apex bank governor had mentioned that the apex bank intended to let the rupee find its own level in the market.
RUPEE SCORES FOUR-MONTH HIGH

The rupee hit a four-month high against the dollar, breaching the 35.8 rupee per dollar mark to end at 35.77 and threatening to erode the competitiveness of Indian exporters. While the Reserve Bank of India remained on the sidelines, watching the appreciation of the Indian currency, traders continued to sell greenbacks even as some expected the RBI to intervene any moment. The main reason for the depreciation of the dollar could be traced to the statement made by the RBI governor in which he said the RBI would be allowing the market to determine the exchange rate.
